g.text: ADR-006: Sign-in and an action → role chart
Status: accepted
Session: —
Cards: —
Exam: —
Supersedes: none
Superseded by: none
Question
one sentence
How do several people use the web interface so that anyone can read, only admins and moderators act, and what each role may do is decided in one
place?
Context
what forces this decision now: facts and constraints, no solutions
• The web interface had no login: it was safe only because it answered on this machine and took form posts only from its own pages.
• To run it for others, the public must be able to browse trials, sponsors and judgements but start, change and spend nothing, in the pages or by
calling the routes (curl, a script).
• Two kinds of people act: admins (sources, model calls that cost money, users) and moderators (curating trials and their evidence). More roles may
come.
• Every write is already audited per core.actor, but every web write was recorded as the account running the server.
• No external services: it runs in Docker Compose next to Postgres.
Options
2–3 real options; the current proposal is only one of them
A. Role checks inside each route
How it works: each route compares the signed-in
user's role with names written in it (if role ==
"admin").
+ smallest change
– the rule is spread over every route; a route
without a check is open and nothing notices
– a new role means editing every route
– nobody can see who may do what
B. One action → role chart in code
How it works: auth/actions.py lists every action and
the roles allowed it. Each route that changes
something names its action (Depends(Requires(...)));
a test fails if one names none. /admin/roles draws
the chart. Users, argon2id password hashes and
sessions are a new auth schema; each user is a
core.actor, so writes are audited as them.
+ one file to read and change; default deny
+ the chart's history is git's
– changing the chart is a code change and a deploy
C. The chart as data
How it works: roles and role_action tables, edited
on an admin page.
+ rules change without a deploy
– more tables and pages to build
– a wrong row opens an action silently; tests can't
see it
– rule changes need versioning (none before
production)
Criteria × options
+ better · 0 no difference · – worse, and a few words why
Criterion
Option A
Option B
Option C
Safety: nothing left unguarded
– a route is easy to forget
+ a test fails on an unguarded route
0 the test can't see the rows
Clarity: who may do what
– read every route
+ one file, one page
+ one page
Effort: to build and to maintain
+ least
0 one module, one test
– tables, admin pages
Traceability: who changed a rule
0 git
+ git; writes as the person
– needs its own audit
Undo: how hard to reverse later
+ drop the auth schema
Decision
what we chose and which criteria decided it
We choose B. Anyone may browse (view); every other action needs a signed-in user whose role the chart allows. Admins may do everything. Moderators
curate: add trials, upload documents, edit sponsors, transfer evidence, run dry-run checks and stop their own jobs. Only admins sync and configure
sources, run checks that call the model (they cost money), stop other people's jobs and manage users. Sign-in is an email and password (argon2id) in
auth.app_user; a session is a random token in an HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax cookie, kept in auth.session only as its SHA-256, ending after 12 hours idle
or 7 days. No sign-up: the first admin comes from TRIALWATCH_ADMIN_EMAIL/_PASSWORD or `user add`. No API tokens yet: the same routes answer a script with 401 or
403. The command line is not limited by roles, since whoever runs it holds the database password. Decided by: safety and clarity.
Consequences
Easier: a new role or action is one line in the chart, and /admin/roles and
the tests follow; the audit log names the person who acted.
Harder: serving it on a network needs HTTPS in front (the cookie is Secure off
this machine) and TRIALWATCH_HOSTS; a forgotten password needs an admin.
Revisit when · Lab
Revisit when: scripts need to act (API tokens on the same chart); a role
should differ per source or trial; sign-in should go through an organisation's
identity provider.
Lab: tests/test_auth.py checks the chart, that every changing route names an
action, each role against the routes, sessions ending, the last admin staying,
and writes recorded as the person.
Session notes
optional
Decided with the user on 2026-11-21: the public browses read-only; password sign-in with sessions in the database; moderators curate data, admins hold
sources, model spend and users; no API tokens for now.
How to use: copy to docs/adr/ADR-NNN-name.excalidraw · replace the grey text (set it to black) · status chip colour: orange open, yellow proposed, green accepted, grey
superseded · one page: if it doesn't fit, the decision is too big, so split it.
